feedback: REJECT. Format is compliant (all headers present, FINAL_STATES nonempty and declared, predicate-only labels, per-state else self-loops give ordered coverage, rewards bounded, all five states reachable), but the machine does not faithfully encode the task 'whenever you are holding the key, the door must be open at that moment or opened afterwards' — the guarantee is mis-encoded in both directions. (1) False failure via absorbing u4: key_lost does not make the task unsatisfiable. Trace: pick up key (u1, +0.1), drop key (key_lost -> u4, -1.0), pick the key up again, toggle the door open, drop the key while the door is open, pick up the box. Every holding moment has a later door opening, so the guarantee holds, yet the RM permanently sits in u4, never reaches u3, and nets -0.9. The agent can re-acquire the key (pickup with empty hands) and the door, once unlocked, is never relocked and can be re-opened without the key, so an absorbing sink keyed to key_lost condemns compliant runs; no regression/recovery transition exits u4. (2) Missed violation via permanent discharge in u2: the obligation re-arms after door regressions. Trace: pick up key (u1), open door (u2, +0.3), toggle the door shut (u2 else, silent), keep holding the key and never re-open until the step limit. The guarantee is violated (holding with the door closed, no later opening), but the RM stays in u2 with zero penalty. u2 conflates 'door has been opened at least once' with 'all obligations discharged'; the property is per-holding-moment and must re-enter a pending state whenever the key is held while the door is closed, including after a close — this task requires explicit regression handling, and the candidate has none (door closing is absorbed by the else self-loop). (3) FINAL_STATES not accepting for the task: u3 is reached by target_picked_up, which the task never mentions; the task is a pure guarantee over has_door_key/door_open/key_lost. A run that satisfies the guarantee but never picks up the box ends in a non-final state, so the acceptance set does not match the task; conversely the RM contains no reward or marker tied to the guarantee's actual satisfaction (e.g., a pending obligation at episode end). (4) Dead transition: (u0, door_open) -> u2 (+0.3) can never fire — the door only opens via a toggle performed while carrying the key, and the key-pickup step already routes u0 -> u1, so u0 never observes door_open; this unfirable transition and its reward entry violate compactness/reachability. (5) Reward safety: -1.0 on key_lost penalizes a move the task permits (dropping the key with the door closed is compliant if the door later opens), and the 0.1/0.3/1.0 chain shapes the box-fetch episode rather than the guarantee itself. Positives to keep: correct handling of the drop-while-door-open case (key_lost false, else loop in u2), event labels used consistently with the persistent/event distinction, and bounded rewards. Rework so that a single door opening discharges all pending obligations and returns the machine to the compliant state, the obligation re-arms on any key-holding with the door closed (including after a regression), key_lost does not lead to an unrecoverable sink, and the accepting condition reflects guarantee compliance rather than box pickup.

TRANSITION_FUNCTION:

(u1, else) -> u1
(u2, target_picked_up) -> u2
(u2, has_door_key & !door_open) -> u3

(u3, target_picked_up & !door_open) -> u3
(u3, else) -> u3
REWARD_FUNCTION:

(u2, target_picked_up, u2) -> 1.0
(u3, target_picked_up & !door_open, u3) -> -1.0
feedback:
Reject. The acceptance skeleton is correct, but the reward layer breaks fidelity and density, and the machine over-specifies the task.

What passes: FINAL_STATES is present, nonempty, declared, and accepting for the task — u0 (no hold-with-closed-door ever occurred; vacuous satisfaction) and u2 (all obligations discharged) are the right accepting states, and u1/u3 rightly reject endings with an undischarged hold. States and INITIAL_STATE are declared; guards are predicate-only and use only the persistent conditions (has_door_key, door_open, target_picked_up); each state has an else self-loop covering irrelevant valuations; listed guards within each state are mutually exclusive, so ordering is safe; key_lost is rightly unused, since a drop with the door closed is not itself a violation (the door may still open afterwards) and the pending states u1/u3 track it correctly; the regression path u2 -> u3 -> u2 is explicitly modeled, which this task needs because door_open can flip false again while the key is held; all four states and all reward edges are reachable (e.g., u3 and its -1.0 edge are reachable by carrying the key through the open door and toggling it shut from the far side); rewards are bounded; the -1.0 edge happens to fire only on violating box-pickup endings and the +1.0 only on satisfying ones, so signs are consistent. Header/tuple format conforms to the paper layout and reward events match declared transition guards.

Defects:
1) Semantic fidelity — out-of-scope rewards. The task is only 'whenever holding the key, the door must be open at that moment or opened afterwards'; it never requires picking up the box. Yet (u2, target_picked_up, u2) -> 1.0 and (u3, target_picked_up & !door_open, u3) -> -1.0 encode the example task 'eventually pick up the target box' (and a door-closed-pickup prohibition) rather than the stated specification. A trace that opens the door and times out fully satisfies the task but is worth only 0.4 under this RM.
2) Reward does not separate satisfying from violating traces; discharge reward is not dense. (u3, door_open, u2) pays nothing while the identical discharge from u1 pays 0.4. Trace 'pickup key, open door (+0.4), toggle the door shut while holding the key (u2 -> u3), timeout' ends non-accepting in u3 yet totals 0.4 — exactly the total of the fully satisfying 'pickup key, open door, timeout' ending in u2. Likewise 'pickup key, never open, timeout' (violating, ends u1) totals 0, equal to the vacuously satisfying do-nothing trace ending in u0. The only penalized ending is the box-pickup one via the out-of-scope -1.0; timeout endings in u1/u3 escape any penalty. Every pending-to-safe discharge is genuine progress and must carry a bounded reward; regression recovery currently has no shaped signal at all.
3) Compactness. The obligation automaton for this property is a pending/no-pending pair (two states). u2 and u3 exist solely to carry the box-pickup +/-1.0; with those removed, u2 collapses into u0 and u3 into u1 behaviorally. The four-state machine over-specifies the task.

Direction (not a rewrite): drop both target_picked_up reward entries, reward discharge uniformly from u1 and u3 on door_open, at which point the machine reduces to the two-state pending/no-pending form this task requires.

REWARD_MACHINE:
STATES: u0, u1
INITIAL_STATE: u0
FINAL_STATES: u0
TRANSITION_FUNCTION:
(u0, has_door_key & !door_open) -> u1
(u0, else) -> u0
(u1, door_open) -> u0
(u1, else) -> u1
REWARD_FUNCTION:
(u0, has_door_key & !door_open, u1) -> -1.0
(u1, door_open, u0) -> 1.0
feedback: The RM faithfully encodes the response property G(has_door_key -> (door_open now / F door_open)). The guard (has_door_key & !door_open) correctly handles 'open at that moment': holding the key while the door is open stays in u0 via the else self-loop with no obligation, while holding it with the door closed enters u1. The pending obligation persists correctly: u1's else self-loop keeps the state through key_lost and target_picked_up, so dropping the key does not discharge the duty and re-picking up the key does not double-penalize; this avoids the common error of exiting u1 on key_lost. door_open from u1 returns to u0, discharging the obligation and permitting new obligations after later door closures or key re-acquisitions, matching the recurring 'whenever' semantics. FINAL_STATES: u0 is present, nonempty, declared, and accepting for the task: vacuous compliance (key never held), full compliance, and 'open at that moment' all end in u0, while violation corresponds exactly to ending in u1 (an undischarged obligation at the last step). Both states are reachable; the 2-state machine is minimal and compact. Guards are predicate-only; in each state the specific guard precedes else, giving correct ordered coverage, and irrelevant propositions (key_lost, target_picked_up) are absorbed by the per-state else self-loops. Rewards are bounded (+/-1.0) and exploitation-free: every +1 (u1->u0) is necessarily preceded by a -1 (u0->u1), so each cycle nets 0 for compliance and the violation path accumulates at most -1; toggling the door shut and re-opening yields no positive-reward farming. Reward is sparse between obligation onset and discharge, but the property has no intermediate milestones beyond these two transitions, so this is as dense as the semantics allow; the -1 on obligation onset gives immediate feedback. Format matches the required layout (REWARD_MACHINE/STATES/INITIAL_STATE/FINAL_STATES/TRANSITION_FUNCTION/REWARD_FUNCTION with correct transition and reward syntax).

Accepted. The function set exactly matches the four environment-declared propositions: has_door_key, door_open, target_picked_up, key_lost — no missing declared predicates and no undeclared extras (target_picked_up and key_lost are unused by this RM but required and correctly present). Each expression matches the documented truth-condition table verbatim: has_door_key checks env.carrying is a key whose color equals a scanned door's color (with None-guards on cells); door_open scans for the single door's is_open; target_picked_up checks carrying.type == 'box' against the mission string built dynamically from the carried color, not a fixed color; key_lost is implemented as an event per the table, reading prev['has_door_key'] from the read-only previous_valuation snapshot and comparing with the current-state K and D expressions inlined exactly as specified (prev true, has_door_key now false, door_open now false), so it fires for one step at the drop and satisfies all declared mutual-exclusion constraints. Persistent propositions (has_door_key, door_open, target_picked_up) read only current state; the previous valuation is only read, never mutated; no imports, no actions, no side effects; only documented API (env.carrying, env.mission, env.grid.get, env.width, env.height, env.episode_memory['previous_valuation']) is used; syntax is valid and all functions return boolean results (the truthiness guard on previous_valuation is a harmless defensive fallback consistent with the documented always-present first-step valuation).
